assist.exactQuestion: Acquire materially new primary or independent evidence reusable by the root owner to close source-addressed underwriting gaps.

claims.claim: Independent Investing.com coverage of Cantor Fitzgerald's post-Q2 review reports Varonis exceeded FactSet consensus across revenue, SaaS ARR, operating income and free cash flow; SaaS ARR excluding conversions grew 25% year over year to $598.1M, NNARR excluding conversions reached $31.5M, and management raised FY2026 SaaS ARR-ex-conversion guidance to $769M-$775M.
claims.materiality: Adds a materially different market/analyst origin from SEC, issuer, BTW, StockAnalysis and Zacks. It independently frames the same operating metrics against FactSet consensus and records an external analyst's interpretation of the guidance raise, giving Alpha another source class for confidence calibration without transferring numeric underwriting authority.

claims.claim: The same independent report says core platform demand plus Atlas, Interceptor and DAM momentum contributed to NNARR excluding conversions, while Varonis remained unprofitable over the trailing twelve months.
claims.materiality: Provides an external execution check that preserves both product-demand evidence and profitability limitation rather than treating SaaS growth as unqualified proof of transition quality.

risks.risk: External analyst coverage remains partly dependent on company-reported quarter metrics; it does not establish customer-level churn, competitive win/loss evidence or fair value.

contradictions.statement: Independent market coverage supports strong SaaS execution and raised guidance while preserving the packet's profitability/transition-quality caveat.

unknowns: Customer-level retention cohorts and competitive displacement remain unobserved.
This evidence does not itself justify changing Alpha's factor, risk, confidence or score values.
recommendedNextState: Reassess the remaining data-confidence failure using this additional independent market/analyst origin together with existing SEC, issuer, transition-analysis, valuation and financial-analysis origins; if still insufficient, change source class to customer/industry evidence rather than another earnings-summary provider.

learning.failedStrategy: Prior independent financial-summary corroboration did not yet close Alpha's data-confidence failure.
learning.changedStrategy: Added a distinct market/analyst source chain anchored to Cantor Fitzgerald interpretation and FactSet consensus rather than another issuer filing or valuation database.
learning.nextLawfulAction: Alpha should test whether the broader origin set now supports its confidence evidence. If not, Scout should switch to customer/industry adoption evidence, not repeat earnings-analysis providers.
